title: activation-integrity-roadmap-and-kpi-sprintpad
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playpad for the next activation window (Q1 pilot -> GA). Focus is on maintaining activation integrity: stable latency and cost per token while scaling users. It combines a roadmap view, KPI trackers, and a lightweight readiness checklist intended for rapid syncs with Eng, SRE, and CS.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Ensure safe ramp from 500 -> 50k daily requests without >5% API error spike or 20% latency regression on p95, and with unit cost delta < 12%.

Context & assumptions:
- Primary customers in pilot: 3 ISV partners, 2 internal product teams.
- Default serving model: redwood/gpt-2b-optim-quant (works with fallback to open/compat-2b).
- Timeline: 6-week runway: week 0 (pilot freeze), week 1-2 (canary), week 3-4 (staged ramp), week 5-6 (GA).

KPI tracker (live values must be pasted from telemetry before each sync):
- p95 latency (ms): target < 450, soft-warning > 550, tripwire > 800
- error rate (5m): target < 0.4%, soft-warning > 1.0%, tripwire > 3.0%
- tokens per request (avg): baseline 180
- unit cost (USD / 1k tokens): baseline 0.28, acceptable bump <= 12%
- cache hit ratio (prefix + KV): target >= 40% for conversational flows
- rollout success ratio (requests served by primary model): target >= 98%

Tripwires & early mitigation heuristics (for on-call and shift leads):
- If p95 > 550ms for 10m: pause new canary cohorts; scale up dedicated pool by +1 node; enable warm-KV preservation policy. Owner: eng-sre on call.
- If error rate > 1.0% for 5m: roll back to previous model variant or route 20% traffic to fallback variant; open incident channel (#activation-integrity). Owner: serving-runtime owner.
- If unit cost exceeds +12% for >24h: throttle non-critical background workloads and re-evaluate batching configs; exec notify required. Owner: product-ops.

Prelaunch checklist (quick run prior to canary profile start):
[ ] Canary traffic definition validated (users, regions, quotas)
[ ] Synthetic smoke tests: cold start p95, streaming integrity, function-call correctness
[ ] Backpressure test passed at 1.5x expected per-node concurrency
[ ] Billing & quota tags applied to canary tokens (to avoid charge leakage)
[ ] CS playbook drafted and validated with partners (support SLAs, rollback messaging)

Runbook excerpts (short actionable snippets):
1) High latency p95 spike
- Immediately enable per-route reduced-batching mode (limits tokens queued per batch)
- If latency remains high after 5m, add temporary autoscale headroom (scale policy: +2 replicas) and notify product-ops
- If >30m and no improvement, initiate controlled rollback to previous model variant

2) Quality regression in canary (model hallucination / structured-output mismatch)
- Run the prompt sample set vs. baseline; if semantic MRR drop > 8% then divert 100% traffic to baseline and begin hotfix prioritization.

Staged rollout roadmap (week-level):
- Week 0: Freeze, finalize canary cohort definitions, CS & legal signoff for partner communications
- Week 1: Canary A (5% traffic, internal partners, single region), 48h observation window
- Week 2: Canary B (20% traffic, multi-region), assess KV cache behavior and token economics
- Week 3: Staged ramp 50% with throttles and throttling guardrails enabled
- Week 4: Full traffic 100% with monitoring escalations, prepare GA checklist
- Week 5-6: GA: post-launch monitoring, burn-down of escalations, support handoff to triage queue

Owner responsibilities (single-line, for quick scanning):
- Product-ops (Samir Patel): rollout coordinator, decisions on traffic gating and cost limits
- Eng-SRE (Lina Gomez): autoscale, infra hotfixes, incident lead during windows
- Serving-runtime (Ethan Morris): model variant rollbacks and runtime flags
- CS & Support (Priya Rao): customer comms, SLA handling, incident triage with partners

Communication templates (short snippets used in Slack/incidents):
- Incident opener: [INC] Activation integrity: p95 620ms, error rate 1.6% — entering mitigation phase. Playbook steps X/Y triggered.
- Partner message (rollback): We’ve detected increased latency for your traffic and are routing you to a stable model variant while we investigate. No action required on your end. ETA 30-90m.

GA acceptance quick gates (final go/no-go):
- All tripwires untriggered for 48h at 50% traffic
- SRE validated autoscale behavior under 2x expected concurrency
- No unresolved P1/P0 incidents in the last 72h
- CS playbook confirmed and on-call notified

Post-launch 30/60/90-day metrics to monitor (for product review):
- Activation retention curve (D1, D7, D30) vs pilot baseline
- Cost per active session (tokens) normalized to throughput band
- Error type breakdown (model errors vs infra vs client misuse)
- Latency percentiles by region and model variant
- Cache efficiency impact on unit economics

Open questions & notes (team use):
- Should we include pre-warmed dedicated nodes in canary to match partner SLAs? (action: engineering feasibility spike, owner: Lina)
- Do we require a separate billing tag for partner preview (legal asked)? (owner: finance contact — cc Priya)
- Need a short eval harness for hallucination checks that runs on each canary deploy (owner: serving-runtime)

Quick links (copy/paste to meeting notes):
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ACT-INT-2025
- Canary plan ticket: JIRA-POPS-987
- Rollout config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-config/pull/45

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc minimal; heavy tables live in the telemetry sheet.
- During preflight, ask product PM for 2 exact customer journeys to validate cache hit targets.

---
End of working pad. Paste recent telemetry snapshots under the KPI tracker before each stand. Replace checkboxes and flag any gate exceptions with short reason strings.
